name: PSECT
short: Declare or resume a code or data section
description: Groups code or data into a named program section. PSECT selects where subsequent instructions, DB/DW data, or DS storage belong. The linker places relocatable sections in memory; absolute sections use fixed addresses. Repeating the same name resumes that section.

operands.name: name
operands.description: Section name, such as myCode. The name identifies the section; it is not a memory address.

operands.name: flag...
operands.description: Optional comma-separated attributes. When resuming an existing section, its name alone is sufficient.

flags.name: class=name
flags.description: Allowed memory range: CODE for instructions; CONST for constants; COMRAM for Access Bank variables; BANK1 for bank 1 variables.

flags.name: space=0 / space=1
flags.description: 0 = program memory (also EEPROM on PIC18); 1 = data memory. Banks share space=1 and are distinguished by their full addresses.

flags.name: delta=1
flags.description: One byte per address unit; use this default for PIC18. DW still emits two bytes per value.

flags.name: reloc=2
flags.description: Start at an even byte address, required for PIC18 executable code. More generally, reloc sets a power-of-two alignment; it does not fix an address.

flags.name: bit
flags.description: Allocate bit-sized objects. DS counts bits and labels hold bit addresses; divide a label by 8 for the byte address and use label & 7 for the bit number.

flags.name: abs
flags.description: Section base is zero and cannot be relocated by the linker. Combine with ovrld and ORG for a fixed location.

flags.name: ovrld
flags.description: Overlay contributions from different source modules instead of concatenating them. Combined with abs, labels have absolute addresses. It does not make overlapping executable contents safe.

flags.name: global / local
flags.description: global is the default: combine same-name sections across modules. local keeps each module's section separate; use a class to place it.

flags.name: size=max
flags.description: Maximum section size, checked after contributions from modules have been combined.

flags.name: limit=address
flags.description: Highest permitted address of the section; checked at link time (PIC18 only).

flags.name: lowdata
flags.description: Keep the whole section below address 0x1000; this is not an Access Bank selector.

flags.name: noexec
flags.description: Mark non-executable contents for debugging. It does not prevent the processor from executing those bytes.

flags.name: pure
flags.description: Declare contents read-only; actual enforcement depends on the target and linker.

flags.name: with=section
flags.description: Place this section in the same memory page as the named section.

flags.name: note
flags.description: Tool/debugger information that is excluded from the final program image.

flags.name: optim=names
flags.description: Colon-separated optimization permissions. Has no effect in standalone pic-as, which performs no optimizations.

flags.name: inline / keep / merge / split
flags.description: Deprecated optimization attributes; the guide uses optim instead. They are not needed for the examples below.

notes: A section name is an identifier, not a memory type or an address. Its attributes and linker class determine placement. A linker class names an allowed range of addresses.

Include <xc.inc> to use predefined sections and linker classes. In PIC18 assembly, the predefined data section holds constants in program memory; it does not create initialized variables in data memory.
DS reserves storage without initializing it. To give a variable an initial value, execute a store instruction, or copy an initial value from program memory.

Resuming a section keeps its attributes. Within one source file, new contents append to that section, even with ovrld. Global sections with the same name normally concatenate across object files; ovrld overlays their contributions instead.
global here concerns section merging; it does not export labels. Use the GLOBAL directive to make a label visible to other source modules.
PSECT itself is processed during assembly and has no processor opcode or execution cycle count.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT myCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
first_value:
    MOVLW 0x2A           ; first routine loads WREG with 0x2A
    RETURN

; Append another routine to the same section.
PSECT myCode
second_value:
    MOVLW 0x00           ; second routine loads WREG with 0
    RETURN
; The linker assigns myCode an even program-memory address.

rows.name: edata (EEDATA)
rows.description: Initial contents to program into the device's EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory).

rows.name: udata (RAM)
rows.description: Uninitialized variables in general-purpose data memory.

rows.name: udata_acs (COMRAM)
rows.description: Uninitialized variables in the Access Bank's general-purpose memory.

rows.name: udata_bankn (BANKN)
rows.description: Uninitialized variables in bank n, for example udata_bank1. The bank must exist on the device.

examples.title: Program-memory constants
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT data
message:
    DB "OK",0             ; bytes: 4F 4B 00
values:
    DW 0x1234             ; bytes: 34 12 on PIC18
; These bytes are stored in program memory.
; Read them with TBLPTR, TBLRD and TABLAT.

examples.title: Access Bank variables
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT udata_acs
counter: DS 1             ; reserve one byte; no initial value

PSECT accessCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
init_counter:
    CLRF counter,0        ; execute to initialize counter to 0
    RETURN

examples.title: Variables in a specific bank
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT udata_bank1
myBuffer: DS 4            ; four bytes in bank 1

PSECT bankCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
store_first:
    BANKSEL myBuffer      ; select the bank containing myBuffer
    MOVLW 0x2A
    MOVWF BANKMASK(myBuffer),1 ; banked access: myBuffer[0] = 0x2A
    RETURN

examples.title: Bit variables
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT bitVars,class=COMRAM,space=1,bit
ready: DS 1               ; reserve one bit, not one byte

PSECT bitCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
clear_ready:
    BCF ready/8,ready&7,0 ; byte address = ready/8; bit = ready&7
    RETURN

examples.title: Fixed reset vector
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT resetVec,class=CODE,abs,ovrld,reloc=2
ORG 0x0000
    GOTO start            ; reset vector at program address 0

PSECT appCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
start:
    BRA start             ; linker places this code elsewhere
; In a relocatable section, ORG is an offset within the section.
; ORG alone does not give a relocatable section a fixed address.

examples.title: Place a relocatable section with the linker
examples.code:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT placedCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
routine:
    RETURN
; At link time, pass this pic-as driver option:
;   -Wl,-PplacedCode=0x200
; This places the section at program address 0x200.
; Do not combine this placement option with an abs section.

name: DB
description: Emits one byte for each numeric value or character into the current program-memory section. A string emits its characters in order.

operands.name: value
operands.description: An 8-bit value, character, or string; separate multiple items with commas.

notes: On PIC18 with delta=1, bytes are consecutive with no padding between them. Strings have no automatic zero terminator; add ,0 when required.
DB does not allocate a variable in data memory. Use DS for storage there. Data bytes must not be reached as executable code.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT data
message:
    DB "OK",0             ; three bytes: 4F 4B 00

PSECT readBytes,class=CODE,reloc=2
read_message:
    MOVLW LOW(message)
    MOVWF TBLPTRL,0
    MOVLW HIGH(message)
    MOVWF TBLPTRH,0
    MOVLW LOW HIGHWORD(message)
    MOVWF TBLPTRU,0
    TBLRD*+               ; TABLAT = 0x4F (O); pointer advances
    TBLRD*+               ; TABLAT = 0x4B (K)
    TBLRD*                ; TABLAT = 0x00 (terminator)
    RETURN

name: DW
description: Emits two bytes for each numeric value or character into the current program-memory section. On PIC18 the low byte comes first.

operands.name: value
operands.description: A 16-bit value, character, or string; each string character occupies a separate 16-bit word.

notes: A PIC18 address unit is still one byte (delta=1); DW determines the width of each emitted value. No automatic string terminator is added.
DW does not reserve data-memory variables. This page documents pic-as; PIC18 behavior in older MPASM code differs.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT data
words:
    DW 0x1234,0xABCD      ; four bytes: 34 12 CD AB

PSECT readWords,class=CODE,reloc=2
read_first_word:
    MOVLW LOW(words)
    MOVWF TBLPTRL,0
    MOVLW HIGH(words)
    MOVWF TBLPTRH,0
    MOVLW LOW HIGHWORD(words)
    MOVWF TBLPTRU,0
    TBLRD*+               ; TABLAT = 0x34 (low byte)
    MOVFF TABLAT,PRODL
    TBLRD*+               ; TABLAT = 0x12 (high byte)
    MOVFF TABLAT,PRODH    ; PRODH:PRODL = 0x1234
    RETURN

name: DS
description: Reserves space in the current section without giving it an initial value. In an ordinary PIC18 data-memory section, count is the number of bytes; in a bit section, it is the number of bits.

operands.name: count
operands.description: Number of address units to reserve; use a data-memory section for variables.

notes: The label identifies the reserved storage. Initialize it by executing instructions; DS 1 does not store the number 1.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT udata_acs
counter: DS 1             ; one uninitialized byte
buffer:  DS 4             ; four uninitialized bytes

PSECT initVars,class=CODE,reloc=2
init_vars:
    CLRF counter,0        ; counter = 0 at runtime
    MOVLW 0x2A
    MOVWF buffer,0        ; first buffer byte = 0x2A
    RETURN

name: EQU
description: Gives a symbol a constant value that the assembler can use in expressions. It emits no data and reserves no storage.

operands.name: symbol
operands.description: New name placed before EQU, with no colon.

operands.name: expression
operands.description: Constant expression to associate with the symbol.

notes: The symbol must not already be defined in the same module. EQU cannot redefine a value; SET is available when redefinition is needed.
EQU creates an assembler symbol. #define replaces source text before assembly and can take arguments; the two mechanisms are different.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

ITEM_COUNT EQU 5
STEP_SIZE  EQU 2

PSECT equCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_count:
    MOVLW ITEM_COUNT      ; WREG = 5
    ADDLW STEP_SIZE       ; WREG = 7
    RETURN
; ITEM_COUNT and STEP_SIZE occupy no data-memory bytes.

name: #define
description: Defines a preprocessor macro: a name that is replaced by source text before the assembler sees it. A macro can also accept parameters.

operands.name: parameters
operands.description: Optional comma-separated names in parentheses immediately after the macro name; no intervening space.

operands.name: replacement
operands.description: Text to substitute; parenthesize expression parameters and the complete expression.

notes: Use a .S source filename (uppercase S), or the pic-as option -xassembler-with-cpp, to enable preprocessing. #define is a preprocessor directive, not an executable instruction.
It allocates no storage. Use EQU for an assembler constant or DS for a variable. End #define at the newline; use C-style comments on its line rather than an assembler semicolon comment.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

#define BASE_VALUE 0x20
#define NEXT_VALUE(x) ((x) + 1)

PSECT defineCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
load_next:
    MOVLW NEXT_VALUE(BASE_VALUE)
    ; After preprocessing: MOVLW ((0x20) + 1)
    ; Executing the instruction sets WREG to 0x21.
    RETURN
